subject: spiny mouse
title: Grab This Mouse and Its Skin Tears Off. Then It Grows Back

scenes.text: Grab this mouse and you're left holding its skin.
It's the African spiny mouse. Its skin is twenty times weaker than a normal mouse's.
It can tear away up to sixty percent of the skin on its back.
Scientists think it's an escape trick: a predator gets a mouthful of skin, not a mouse.
Then the strange part. Within a day, a big wound has shrunk by about two thirds.
New skin grows in, hair and all. It's the first mammal known to shed its skin like a lizard drops its tail.

description:
African spiny mice (Acomys kempi and Acomys percivali) from Kenya have skin that tears away when they are grabbed, and then grows back.
A 2012 study in Nature measured their skin at about 20 times weaker than a lab mouse's, taking nearly 77 times less energy to break. They can lose around 60 percent of the skin on their backs; large wounds shrank by 64 percent within 24 hours and regrew hair follicles, and holes punched in their ears refilled with skin, hair and cartilage. It was the first skin shedding of this kind shown in a mammal; its use against predators is based on field reports.
Which animal has the best escape trick? Comment below.
thumbnail_text: ITS SKIN TEARS OFF. ON PURPOSE.
first_comment: Holes four millimetres wide punched in their ears closed up again, cartilage and hair included. Lizard tail or mouse skin: which trick wins?
